title: Fluid Dynamics
description: Water, air and magma all obey one equation, and one number tells which way it goes: below a Reynolds number of about 2300 a pipe flows in smooth layers, above it the flow breaks into eddies. Unlocks the Laminar Flow Conduit.

puzzle.goal: A fluid of density ρ and viscosity μ moves at speed v past a body of length L. Inertia carries it on, viscosity damps it out; their ratio decides whether it flows smooth or turbulent. Write R, the Reynolds number (Re in the books).
puzzle.name: Reynolds number
puzzle.ask: Find R for water in a pipe: ρ = @{ρ} kg/m³, v = @{v} m/s, L = @{L} m, μ = @{μ} Pa·s. Below about 2300 it stays laminar.
puzzle.method: Inertial force per volume goes as ρv²/L and viscous force as μv/L²; divide one by the other.
